sections.h2: What is the fastest path to a closing in Homestead, FL?
sections.html:
Choose a buyer type, line up the title and lien paperwork, then sign a deed that is witnessed, taxed and recorded in Miami-Dade County. The pace comes from the buyer and the cleanliness of title, not from skipping recording steps.

South Dade sellers usually compare three routes. A retail listing draws the widest crowd yet waits on a lender's appraisal. A cash purchase removes the lender and often the repair haggling, which suits houses that need work. A family sale is allowed, though a transfer for money still carries deed tax, and the revenue department notes there is no separate exemption for estate-planning transfers.

  • Confirm who is on title, including any owner who has died or moved away.
  • Ask each lender for a payoff letter.
  • Request the current tax bill and check for unpaid prior years.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Homestead's history and growth?
sections.html:
Homestead calls itself the second oldest city in Miami-Dade County. South Dade opened to homesteaders in 1898, and Henry Flagler's decision to extend the railroad to Key West in 1904 brought workers who stayed. The Town of Homestead was incorporated in 1913 with 121 residents and 28 registered voters, and the state granted it city status in 1923.

Later chapters shaped what buyers see today. A military airfield opened in 1942 and the air force base was reestablished in 1953. Turkey Point Nuclear Power Station was commissioned in 1972, and Hurricane Andrew hit the city directly in 1992. The Speedway broke ground in 1993 and held its first race in 1995. More recent milestones in the city's timeline include a voter-approved downtown revitalization in 2014, the Seminole Theatre reopening in 2015, a new City Hall in 2016 and the Cybrarium library in 2021.

Census QuickFacts shows growth from 60,512 residents in 2010 to 80,737 in 2020 and an estimate of 86,242 for mid-2025.

Details from the timeline show how long the community has been mixed. Lawrence and Rebecca McClain platted McClain's Addition in 1913, Fannie Showers Starr opened the first formal school for African American children in 1924, and Ed Leedskalnin began Coral Castle in 1926. Royal Palm State Park became Everglades National Park in 1947. The city also lists designated historic districts and a historic downtown, so check with the city before altering an older building.

With a hurricane of that scale in the city's record, keep your permit history and any insurance claim paperwork handy for the buyer and the title agent.

sections.h2: What should a Homestead owner know about local housing figures?
sections.html:
These figures describe a young, family-heavy market where renting is common. Across 2020 to 2024 Census surveys, 48.3 percent of Homestead homes had owner residents, so rentals edge ahead. Homes that owners live in are valued at a median of $380,000, and the middle rent is $1,674.

  • Household size: 3.21 people on average, well above the typical city figure.
  • Age: under-18s are 29.5 percent of residents, while seniors account for just 8.5 percent.
  • Home languages: 68.8 percent of residents aged five and up use a tongue besides English at home, so bilingual listings and documents help.
  • Commute: workers average 35.8 minutes to get to work.

Median household income is $65,423, and the city's 2022 retail sales per capita were $12,343. Those figures suggest buyers who compare monthly cost closely, so price and condition drive offers.

sections.h2: How does renting affect selling a Homestead house?
sections.html:
Plenty of sellers here are landlords or heirs who have no history of living in the house, which matters for tax and for the buyer's questions.

Miami-Dade's property appraiser tells owners not to jeopardize a homestead exemption by renting the property. If an exemption was claimed while the home was rented, the office says back taxes can reach ten years, with 15 percent annual interest and a 50 percent penalty. Raise that with a Florida attorney before you sell.

If a tenant occupies the house, give the buyer the lease early. Under Chapter 83 a periodic tenancy by the month needs 30 days of notice, and an unpaid-rent demand runs three days, leaving out weekends and court holidays.

sections.h2: How is a deed taxed in Homestead, and who must sign?
sections.html:
Homestead sits in Miami-Dade, where the revenue department lists a different deed rate: 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that is not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling. Other counties charge 70 cents.

That carve-out is why the property type matters. A single-family house generally avoids the surtax, while a duplex does not fit the description. Your closing agent should confirm which applies.

Whoever signs the deed shares liability for the tax however the contract splits it, paid to the clerk at filing. Clerk fees under section 28.24 start at $5.00 for a first page. A conveyance of land must be written and signed before two subscribing witnesses, and the statute allows audio-video witnessing.

sections.h2: What does Miami-Dade say about homestead after a sale?
sections.html:
The seller's exemption ends and each new owner files separately. Miami-Dade's property appraiser says applications are due March 1, with late filings accepted until the cutoff named on the TRIM notice, generally 25 days after it is mailed. A $15 fee may apply to late filings that need a Value Adjustment Board petition.

That page also reports that voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026. It states the maximum non-school exemption rises to $150,000 for tax year 2027 and $250,000 for 2028 for owners who established Florida residency by December 31, 2026, with different rules for later arrivals, and that the school-board exemption stays $25,000. Ask the appraiser how this applies to your buyer.

After closing, the next January 1 brings a fresh just-value assessment, so the buyer's first bill can exceed yours. Afterward the cap limits yearly growth to 3 percent or CPI change, whichever is smaller.

sections.h2: What if liens, a foreclosure or an estate are involved?
sections.html:
• Foreclosure: the clerk's sale follows a final judgment by 20 to 35 days unless the plaintiff consents to longer.
  • Probate: a small estate (non-exempt value up to $150,000) or a death more than two years back can use summary administration.
  • Tax certificates: once two years pass from April 1 of the issue year, the holder can ask for a tax deed, so clear old balances first.

Deaths after 2004 trigger no Florida estate tax.

faqs.q: Is the deed tax different in Homestead?
faqs.a: Yes. Miami-Dade County, where the city lies, has its own schedule. The rate is 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents surtax that does not apply when only a single-family dwelling transfers.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Homestead house with a tenant inside?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer takes it subject to the lease, so share a copy. Tenancies without a fixed term end on statutory notice, such as 30 days for month-to-month.

faqs.q: Does the buyer get my exemption?
faqs.a: No. The buyer must file by March 1, and assessed value resets after the ownership change.

faqs.q: How are unpaid property taxes handled?
faqs.a: The closing agent pays them from your proceeds. The Miami-Dade tax collector can give you the amount owed; unpaid taxes unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1.

faqs.q: How long does the deed take to record?
faqs.a: Recording happens at the clerk's office, where the stamp tax is also paid. Speed depends on the clerk's queue and whether your closing agent files electronically.
